# Miqsat Ma'ase Ha-Torah Section 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 4QMMT (4Q394–399, Cave 4), Section B concluded + beginning of C | **Condition:** Fragmentary; reconstructed from multiple manuscripts

---

**5:1** Regarding [...] the women of Israel and the preservation of the holy bloodline [...] no one should [...] a woman who sells her body [...]

**5:2** [...] because [...] the holy bloodline of the priestly descendants of Aaron [...] and the people of Israel as well [...]

**5:3** [...] The holy bloodline must not be allowed to mix with [...] and no one should allow [...]

**5:4** [...] because they are holy [...] and Scripture says: "You must not bring a prostitute's wages into the house of the LORD your God" [...]

**5:5** Regarding the tenth-portion of the grain, the wine, and the oil: the priests should be [...] the first to receive the first fruits [...]

**5:6** [...] and the Levites [...] are to collect the tenth-portion [...] from the Israelites [...]

**5:7** [...] And regarding the tenth-portion of the tenth-portion [...] the priests are to receive their share from the Levites [...]

**5:8** [...] because [...] we believe the grain tithe is equivalent to the first fruits [...] and belongs to the priests [...]

**5:9** [...] No one should hold back the tithe [...] because these are sacred contributions [...]

**5:10** Regarding [...] no Ammonite, Moabite, person of forbidden birth, or eunuch may enter the worshiping community [...]

**5:11** [...] and they must not [...] marry anyone from these groups [...] nor should they be allowed in [...]

**5:12** [...] because [...] the LORD's worshiping community is holy [...] and Scripture says [...]

**5:13** [...] Regarding anyone with a skin disease [...] a person afflicted with a serious skin condition [...] must not come near anything connected with the temple's holiness [...]

**5:14** [...] not until the sun sets on the eighth day [...] after being declared clean [...]

**5:15** You are well aware that we have cut ourselves off from the main body of the peo[ple and from all] their impurity,

**5:16** and from having any part in these practices or participating [...] in any of them [...]

**5:17** [...] and you know that none of us [...] has been unfaithful in any of these matters [...]

**5:18** [...] because [...] it was for the sake of these very issues that we separated [...]

**5:19** [...] and we have [...] pulled away from the general population [...] and from all their corrupt practices [...]

**5:20** We have also [...] written to you so that you will study the books of Moses [and the writings of the Prophets and of David...]

**5:21** [...] and the records of every generation [...] and in those writings it says [...]

**5:22** [...] that [...] you would stray from the right path [...] and that disaster would overtake you [...]

**5:23** [...] as it is written: "When all these things have happened to you" [...]

**5:24** [...] "in the final days, both the blessing and the curse" [...]

**5:25** [...] "then you will take it to heart and return to Him with all your heart and all your being" [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: Section B's final rulings and the transition to Section C are rendered for maximum clarity. "Holy bloodline" renders zera' qodesh dynamically, emphasizing the genealogical concern. "Sells her body" clarifies zonah for modern readers (though the traditional "prostitute" appears in the Deuteronomy citation). "Tenth-portion" explains ma'aser concretely before using "tithe." "Person of forbidden birth" renders mamzer without the harsh connotation of "bastard." "Skin disease" replaces "leprosy" since biblical tsara'at likely refers to various conditions, not Hansen's disease. Section C's "cut ourselves off" vividly conveys the radical nature of the separation. "All your being" renders nephesh dynamically (vs. the traditional "soul").*
